mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate indicates labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is high and unemployment is low, it may signal tightening monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500.
failure_condition: If the condition is met but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth supports economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate stimulates economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Declining retail sales indicate weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If retail sales decline but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment and decreasing unemployment indicate a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 50k and UNRATE decreases by 0.5pp
failure_condition: If labor market improves but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rate during economic expansion signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.
